instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Propose a general comparison method independently, before seeing the author's rules or any disputed reading.

content.text: {"written_text_status":"Treat the shared unpointed consonantal text as fixed for this comparison unless the task separately permits emendation or a consonantal textual variant. Vocalization, word division, morphology, syntax, and sense must be evaluated without silently changing, adding, deleting, or transposing consonants.","admissibility_gate":["The candidate exactly accounts for the stipulated consonants in their stipulated order, allowing only orthographic phenomena independently attested for the relevant language, period, and corpus.","The proposed vocalization and segmentation instantiate an attested or regularly productive morphological pattern; merely imaginable forms do not pass.","The resulting construction is grammatically possible in the relevant Hebrew or Aramaic variety. Rare constructions require actual parallels or a clearly applicable productive rule.","The proposed lexeme and sense are attested in an appropriate source or follow a normal, independently evidenced semantic extension. A root-level resemblance alone is insufficient.","The candidate yields a minimally coherent clause in its immediate literary context without requiring unmarked ellipsis, exceptional syntax, and an unattested sense simultaneously.","All exceptional assumptions must be stated explicitly. A candidate passes only if each exception has independent evidence rather than being invented to rescue that candidate."],"hard_disqualifiers":["Failure to account for the fixed consonants without an expressly permitted textual emendation.","Dependence on a morphological form or syntactic construction that is impossible under the relevant language system, rather than merely rare.","Dependence on a lexical sense for which there is neither attestation nor a regular and contextually defensible semantic derivation.","Internal incompatibility among the candidate's own morphology, syntax, and proposed translation.","Dependence on mutually inconsistent analyses, such as assigning the same element incompatible grammatical functions.","A claimed historical or orthographic mechanism contradicted by securely established chronology or by the stipulated textual state."],"comparison_rules":[{"rule_id":"R1","title":"Separate admissibility from preference","operation":"HARD_CONSTRAINT","rule":"First apply the admissibility gate to each candidate independently. Do not treat the survival of both candidates as evidence that they are equally probable.","justification":"Logical possibility is a threshold question; comparative support is a separate inquiry."},{"rule_id":"R2","title":"Analyze the local clause first","operation":"COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT","rule":"Compare how naturally each candidate fits the immediate clause and nearby discourse: argument structure, agreement, government, constituent relations, reference, information structure, collocation, genre, and discourse progression. Count ordinary, directly attested constructions over analyses requiring accumulated exceptions.","justification":"The immediate linguistic environment most directly constrains the missing vocalization."},{"rule_id":"R3","title":"Use grammar comparatively, not merely permissively","operation":"COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT","rule":"After excluding impossible analyses, prefer the candidate using the more regular construction for the relevant corpus and period. Rarity is adverse evidence only when frequency estimates use a defined comparison class and do not confuse absence in a small corpus with impossibility.","justification":"Both readings may be grammatical while differing substantially in constructional probability."},{"rule_id":"R4","title":"Evaluate lexical fit by sense and collocation","operation":"COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT","rule":"Prefer the lexeme and sense that are better attested with the relevant subjects, objects, prepositions, semantic domain, and genre. Dictionary inclusion establishes admissibility, not equal probability. Gloss counts or the number of lexicons repeating the same evidence must not be treated as independent votes.","justification":"Lexicons summarize evidence; contextual distribution and collocation distinguish possible senses from likely ones."},{"rule_id":"R5","title":"Prioritize controlled authorial usage","operation":"SOURCE_WEIGHT","rule":"Use repeated, unambiguous examples from the same book or coherent compositional stratum as strong comparative evidence, especially when the same form, construction, or collocation recurs. Control for genre, speaker, date, dialect, and possible redactional diversity.","justification":"Usage within the closest linguistic population is generally more probative than remote analogy."},{"rule_id":"R6","title":"Use broader parallels with decreasing proximity","operation":"SOURCE_WEIGHT","rule":"When local and whole-book evidence do not decide the issue, consult progressively less proximate corpora: same authorial or linguistic stratum, closely related books and genres, then wider biblical Hebrew or Aramaic. Canonical status alone does not make a parallel linguistically close.","justification":"Parallels are informative in proportion to linguistic, chronological, generic, and constructional comparability."},{"rule_id":"R7","title":"Distinguish genuine parallels from thematic resemblance","operation":"COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT","rule":"A parallel is probative only to the extent that it shares the relevant lexeme, morphology, syntax, collocation, discourse function, or demonstrable source relationship. General thematic similarity is weak evidence for vocalization.","justification":"Theme can support interpretation without identifying the linguistic form."},{"rule_id":"R8","title":"Treat manuscript evidence according to what it preserves","operation":"SOURCE_WEIGHT","rule":"Unpointed manuscripts normally confirm consonants but do not directly distinguish vocalizations. Pointed, partially pointed, transliterated, orthographically disambiguating, or explicitly annotated manuscripts may support a reading. Evaluate their date, provenance, independence, correction history, and whether the notation is original or secondary.","justification":"A witness has force only for features it actually encodes."},{"rule_id":"R9","title":"Retrovert ancient translations cautiously","operation":"SOURCE_WEIGHT","rule":"Use an ancient translation only when the target-language rendering materially distinguishes the candidates and a plausible retroversion favors one. Reduce its force for free translation, paraphrase, harmonization, target-language ambiguity, uncertain Vorlage, or translator inconsistency. Establish translator habits from a defined sample where possible.","justification":"Translations are indirect witnesses to interpretation and sometimes to text, not transparent transcriptions of vowels."},{"rule_id":"R10","title":"Group dependent evidence","operation":"HARD_CONSTRAINT","rule":"Place witnesses deriving from a shared exemplar, recension, translation tradition, lexical database, or interpretive tradition into one evidentiary family. Do not count descendants, revisions, or modern repetitions as independent confirmations unless they preserve demonstrably independent information.","justification":"Uncorrected dependence creates false numerical majorities."},{"rule_id":"R11","title":"Apply a fixed qualitative hierarchy","operation":"COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT","rule":"Within the fixed consonantal-text problem, use this default order: direct disambiguating textual evidence; immediate morphology, syntax, and tightly constrained context; securely comparable whole-book usage; proximate corpus usage; independently early interpretive witnesses; broader canonical parallels; remote analogies and modern judgments. A lower level may corroborate but ordinarily does not overturn clear higher-level evidence without a specific transmission or corruption explanation.","justification":"A predeclared hierarchy prevents selective promotion of congenial evidence."},{"rule_id":"R12","title":"Record evidence in an auditable ledger","operation":"REPORTING","rule":"For each candidate, list every material datum, its evidentiary family, proximity, direction, strength, and known uncertainty. Record contrary evidence as well as favorable evidence, and state which observations are shared rather than independent.","justification":"A common ledger makes omissions, double-counting, and post hoc weighting visible."},{"rule_id":"R13","title":"Decision threshold","operation":"REPORTING","rule":"Declare one reading better supported only if it passes the gate and either has controlling evidence or has a clear advantage at the highest evidentiary level that materially distinguishes the candidates, with no comparably strong unresolved counterevidence. If the advantage depends only on several weak or dependent indicators, report underdetermination.","justification":"The method should permit conclusions without converting small accumulations of weak evidence into false certainty."}],"evidence_hierarchy":[{"evidence":"Fixed consonantal text and securely encoded distinctions in relevant manuscripts","default_role":"CONTROLLING","conditions":"Controlling only for features actually preserved and within the stipulated textual problem; consonantal witnesses alone usually cannot control vowel choice."},{"evidence":"Immediate morphology, clause syntax, argument structure, and tightly constraining local discourse","default_role":"STRONG","conditions":"Apply symmetrically and distinguish impossibility from markedness or rarity."},{"evidence":"Repeated, unambiguous usage in the same book or coherent linguistic stratum","default_role":"STRONG","conditions":"Examples must be genuinely comparable and not all instances of the disputed form."},{"evidence":"Masoretic vowel points and associated reading tradition","default_role":"STRONG","conditions":"They are direct evidence for a carefully transmitted reading tradition but are later than the consonantal text and therefore rebuttable concerning the earliest recoverable reading."},{"evidence":"Masoretic accents","default_role":"SUPPORTING","conditions":"Useful for the received syntactic and prosodic analysis; evaluate together with, not independently from, the Masoretic vocalization tradition."},{"evidence":"Ketiv/Qere notation","default_role":"CONTEXT_DEPENDENT","conditions":"Strong evidence that a recognized written/read distinction existed in the Masoretic tradition, but its bearing on the earliest text depends on the individual case and transmission history."},{"evidence":"Comparable usage in linguistically, chronologically, and generically proximate biblical material","default_role":"SUPPORTING","conditions":"Strength increases with exact morphological, syntactic, and collocational correspondence."},{"evidence":"Broader canonical parallels","default_role":"WEAK","conditions":"May become supporting when correspondence is linguistically exact or a literary dependence is independently demonstrated; canonical status by itself adds no linguistic weight."},{"evidence":"Ancient translations or transliterations","default_role":"CONTEXT_DEPENDENT","conditions":"Potentially strong when early, independent, literal at the relevant point, and unambiguously distinguishing; otherwise supporting or weak."},{"evidence":"Lexicons and grammars","default_role":"SUPPORTING","conditions":"Use as documented syntheses and pathways to primary examples. Their labels and citations matter more than the number of reference works agreeing."},{"evidence":"Modern translations, commentarial popularity, denominational authority, or unspecified scholarly consensus","default_role":"EXCLUDED","conditions":"May identify arguments or primary evidence but cannot serve as independent evidence or a vote."},{"evidence":"Theological desirability, doctrinal convenience, or compatibility with a preferred outcome","default_role":"EXCLUDED","conditions":"May describe reception history but cannot decide the linguistic reading."}],"received_pointing_role":"REBUTTABLE_PRESUMPTION","received_pointing_rule":"When a stable received pointing exists, begin with it as a historically transmitted reading rather than a neutral modern conjecture. The challenger bears a production burden to present specific evidence favoring departure. This presumption is not binding and weakens where the pointing is late, divided, secondary, grammatically strained, contradicted by earlier independent evidence, or plausibly generated by a known interpretive or scribal tendency. Points and accents from the same tradition must not be counted as independent witnesses.","burden_of_proof_rule":"The gate is symmetrical: every candidate must establish consonantal, morphological, grammatical, lexical, and contextual admissibility. Comparative burdens are asymmetric only when one candidate is directly attested by a received or earlier reading tradition and the other is reconstructed: the reconstructed candidate must show a material evidentiary advantage sufficient to overcome that attestation. No candidate receives a burden advantage merely because it supports a familiar theology, modern majority, simpler translation, or evaluator preference. Anyone alleging corruption, deliberate alteration, exceptional dialect, or special genre license bears the burden of documenting that mechanism independently.","dependent_witness_rule":"Identify genealogical and functional dependence before aggregation. Manuscripts from one recension, daughter translations, revisions of an earlier version, Masoretic points and accents, lexicons citing the same examples, and commentators repeating one proposal form single evidence clusters. Report both the number of extant witnesses and the smaller number of independent evidentiary families, but base comparative force primarily on the latter. Agreement produced by a shared ambiguous source is not independent confirmation of a particular vocalization.","source_bias_rule":"Do not discount a source merely because it is Jewish, Christian, sectarian, traditional, or modern. Discount or adjust only for a specified, testable mechanism relevant to the passage type, such as systematic harmonization, euphemistic substitution, anti-anthropomorphism, liturgical normalization, doctrinal revision, target-language convention, or mechanical copying. Establish the tendency from independent examples, apply it equally to congenial and uncongenial readings, and distinguish motive speculation from demonstrated textual behavior.","special_context_rules":["Identify genre, date, dialect, speaker, and register before invoking special usage; the classification must be supported independently of the desired reading.","In poetry, allow documented ellipsis, parallelism, inversion, rare vocabulary, and sound patterning, but do not use 'poetic license' to excuse an otherwise unsupported analysis.","For quotations, allusions, and harmonized passages, distinguish the wording of the present text from influence by the source or a parallel tradition.","For Aramaic passages, code-switching, loanwords, and mixed linguistic environments, use the grammar and lexicon of the relevant variety rather than importing Hebrew or later Aramaic patterns without evidence.","For pausal, dialectal, archaic, or late forms, require comparable forms from an independently identified corpus or a productive historical rule.","For proper names, technical terms, wordplay, and deliberate ambiguity, permit multiple activated senses only when the form and context independently signal that phenomenon; do not use wordplay as a universal escape from choosing.","Where scribal taboo, euphemism, liturgical substitution, or correction is alleged, require evidence of the practice and a plausible transmission path in the relevant tradition."],"tie_rule":"Report 'underdetermined' when both candidates pass the gate and neither has controlling evidence or a clear advantage at the highest material, independent evidentiary level. Do not break a tie by counting dependent witnesses, by preferring the interpretation with greater theological coherence, by assuming that older is automatically original, or by appealing to mere simplicity without defining it. If a forced provisional choice is required, select the reading with fewer independently unsupported assumptions and label it explicitly as low-confidence and provisional.","anti_ad_hoc_safeguards":["Freeze the admissibility criteria, evidence hierarchy, burden rules, and decision threshold before learning the disputed reading or desired outcome.","Use the same corpus boundaries, date ranges, grammatical categories, and definition of a parallel for both candidates.","Predefine search procedures and report search terms, databases, editions, exclusions, and negative searches so that corpus claims can be reproduced.","Maintain a full evidence ledger including adverse, neutral, ambiguous, and favorable data; do not report only examples supporting the selected reading.","Separate primary observations from inferences and from judgments copied from secondary sources.","Do not introduce numerical weights after inspection. If numerical scoring is ever used, define and validate the scale in advance and accompany it with sensitivity analysis.","Perform a reversal check: replace the candidate labels and confirm that the same facts would receive the same classifications and weights.","Perform an ablation check: state whether the conclusion survives removal of each dependent evidence family and each disputed contextual assumption.","Document every departure from the default hierarchy with a general rule that would apply to comparable cases regardless of outcome.","Preserve an underdetermined category; the method must not force selection whenever the evidence lacks discriminatory power."],"proposed_baseline":"Apply a constrained, hierarchical likelihood comparison. First hold the consonantal text fixed and admit only candidates satisfying independent orthographic, morphological, grammatical, lexical, and minimal contextual requirements. Then compare candidates at the highest evidence level that genuinely distinguishes them, prioritizing direct encoded evidence and immediate linguistic constraints, followed by controlled same-book and proximate-corpus usage. Treat the received pointing as a rebuttable historical presumption, ancient translations as indirect and translator-dependent, lexicons and grammars as syntheses rather than votes, and broad parallels as corroborative. Cluster dependent witnesses, state exceptions and transmission hypotheses explicitly, and choose a reading only when the independent evidence shows a clear advantage; otherwise report underdetermination.","clarifications_needed":["Whether the consonantal text is absolutely stipulated or whether consonantal variants and emendations may be considered in a separate analysis.","Which textual edition and manuscript corpus define the base consonants and witness set.","What chronological and dialectal corpus boundaries are appropriate for the material under study.","Whether the task seeks the earliest recoverable vocalization, the reading of a specified historical community, the received reading, or the best synchronic linguistic interpretation; these are distinct targets.","Whether a forced provisional choice is required when the evidence is underdetermined."],"confidence":"HIGH"}
